title: the oldest the most expensive
subtitle: the biggest / the most expensive
summary: Use the -est or the most ... to say that one thing is more than all the others.

lesson.heading: Comparative and superlative
lesson.text: Four boxes stand in a line: A is the big one, then B, then D, and C is very small. Box A is **bigger than** Box B. Box A is **bigger than** all the other boxes, so Box A is **the biggest** box. It works the same way with hotel prices. The Europa costs 140 pounds a night, the Grand 125 and the Station only 75.

examples.text: The Europa Hotel is **more expensive than** the Grand.
The Europa Hotel is **more expensive than** all the other hotels in the city.
The Europa Hotel is **the most expensive** hotel in the city.

lesson.note: *bigger / older / more expensive* are **comparative** forms. *biggest / oldest / most expensive* are **superlative** forms.

lesson.heading: How to make the superlative
lesson.note: Spelling: big -> the bi**gg**est, hot -> the ho**tt**est. Words ending in *-y* change to *-iest*.

lesson.heading: We say the oldest / the most expensive
lesson.text: The superlative nearly always has **the** in front of it.

examples.text: The church is very old. It's **the oldest** building in the town.
examples.note: = it is older than all the other buildings

examples.text: What is **the longest** river in the world?
Money is important, but it isn't **the most important** thing in life.
Excuse me, where is **the nearest** bank?

lesson.heading: Superlative without a noun
lesson.text: You can use **the oldest / the best / the most expensive** without a noun, when it is clear what you are talking about.

examples.text: Ken is a good player, but he isn't **the best** in the team.

lesson.heading: the best I've ever ...
lesson.text: We often use a superlative with **I've ever ...** or **you've ever ...** to talk about all our life until now.

examples.text: The film was very bad. I think it's **the worst** film **I've ever seen**.
What is **the most unusual** thing **you've ever done**?

lesson.text: Don't forget **the**: *she's the youngest*, not ~~she's youngest~~.

exercises.prompt: Box A is bigger than all the other boxes. Box A is ___.
exercises.explanation: Short word: the + adjective + -est, with the last letter written twice.

exercises.prompt: Line B is shorter than lines A, C and D. Line B is ___.
exercises.explanation: short is a short word, so the superlative is the shortest.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective with its superlative.
A is 23, B is 19, C is 24 and D is 21. B is ___.
exercises.explanation: B is younger than all the others, so B is the youngest.

exercises.prompt: Which superlative does each adjective take?
Vase A costs 8 pounds, B costs 10, C costs 15 and D costs 12. C is ___ vase.
exercises.explanation: expensive is a long word, so we say the most expensive.

exercises.prompt: Vase A costs 8 pounds, B costs 10, C costs 15 and D costs 12. A is ___ vase.
exercises.explanation: A costs less than all the others, so A is the cheapest.

exercises.prompt: Restaurant A is excellent. Restaurant D is awful. Which sentence is right?
exercises.explanation: bad is irregular: bad - worse - the worst.

exercises.prompt: It was a very happy day. It was ___ of my life.
exercises.explanation: happy ends in -y, so the superlative is the happiest.

exercises.prompt: It's a very good film. It's ___ I've ever seen.
exercises.explanation: good is irregular: good - better - the best.

exercises.statement: The Nile is the most long river in Africa.
exercises.explanation: The Nile is the longest river in Africa. long is a short word, so we add -est.

exercises.prompt: No mountain in the world is higher than Everest. Put the sentence in order.
exercises.answer: Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
